claim_class: Integer-mode mutual-inverse claim pair: an affine bijection between the two integer-feasible sets that preserves the objective pointwise (hence the extended infimum on the integer domain) over the 6,846 retained coordinates. Both claims are {input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal'} with forward reverse:false/inverse:1 and reverse:true/inverse:0. The continuous relaxation is deliberately out of scope, and no improvement, strictness, point or bijection claim is declared.
claims: Two claim records, byte-identical to the RPA's claims array (175,996 B of RPA text vs request.json 175,997 B): forward {reverse:false, input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal', projection:[[src,tgt] x 6846], inverse:1} and its transposed twin {reverse:true, ..., projection:[[tgt,src] x 6846], inverse:0} - a mutual-inverse pair over exactly the 6,846 coordinates the target keeps.

Payload economics: each claim serializes to 87,996-87,997 B, of which 87,889 B (99.9%) is the enumerated projection table and only about 107 B are the five scope/strength fields (reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective, inverse). The whole 87,889 B follows from one fact - retained coordinates are shared and unmodified - yet it is written twice and again inside the RPA.

Explicitly absent: no improvements, points or bijections - verify reports bijections 0, points 0 (cases/test64/preparation.json kernel_runs[3]); the contract string says 'No LP equality, LP inclusion, global strictness, feasibility or optimum claim.' (cases/test64/preparation.json 'claims'); there is no README.md in cases/test64.

Why integer mode is load-bearing, not stylistic: the 40.7%-of-RPA alias family proves x1=x2=y from x1+x2-2y=0 by Cases on a binary y, and the LP relaxation admits (1,0,1/2) ('Exact binary equivalence is not continuous equivalence', /tmp/rpx-digests/test64.md report section 3 rejected hypotheses); LP-mode integrality premises are rejected by the kernel (crates/core/src/verify.rs:178, crates/core/src/verify.rs:205).

agent_manual_work: Hand-written exact MPS parser over the 174,587-line, 10,089,711 B source (sections, INTORG/INTEND nesting, D exponents, duplicate-coefficient summing, explicit BV/LI coverage) plus a second, independent parser inside the 13,016 B output/verify.py; 52,086 characters of eval code in 14 cells, no solver and no framework members (solver-blind baseline).

All structure discovery by hand with Fraction and stdlib counters: 6,875 three-term rows x1+x2-2y=0 with truth table {(0,0,0),(1,1,1)}, 275 identical opposite-sense pairs, 550 w-equations matching those pairs after alias substitution, 600 linkYQCut rows equal to the negative of a retained linkXQ equality, 69 assignment equalities as exact linear combinations, six cost definitions, zero identical columns.

Ordered saturation fixpoint: exact interval/extremum evaluation per row, 680 certificates in four rounds (1204, 1564, 48, 0 new fixings) establishing 2,816 fixed coordinates (y 0:1675; q 1:200 / 0:80; a 0:520 / 1:96; u 1:13; p 1:48 / 0:16; hRTGT 0:168).

2,546 bound-entailment deletions with explicit infinite endpoints, then gcd/sign canonicalization for normalized duplicate detection after fixings; everything recorded in a 7,774,166 B audit.json that the kernel preparer consumes as raw dict keys.

One failed hypothesis (the run's single failing call): the aggregate cutQ(T1) identity broke because duration-two groups carry coefficient 1 at boundary slots and 2 elsewhere (AssertionError), so the 16 surviving cutQ rows were kept and the residual formulation recomputed without it.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test64.py (177 lines) defs: cases_eq(:13), drop_dead(:22 with nested refs(:25)), prepare(:47 with nested branch(:53), normalize(:63), recover(:134)); the raw-dict mutation list for the three negative checks sits at :176 inside __main__.

Imports six sibling preparers: run_receipt (prepare_test45), row_ref (prepare_affine), expression/plus/mul/expr_json/row_fact (prepare_test40), substitute (prepare_test57), SparseBuilder (prepare_test70), box/exact (prepare_test54) - a 999-line transitive helper stack under 177 lines of case code.
SparseBuilder (prepare_test70) is the whole de-facto proof API: it allocates ids, evaluates refexpr/kind and appends raw step dicts; the kernel only ever sees 'RPA 2' text.

run_receipt (tools/prepare_test45.py:13-48) is the de-facto compiler driver: resolves the run's source/target MPS and audit.json, emits the RPA, writes request.json = cert['claims'], runs canonical/assemble/verify, three mutation negative checks and two determinism re-verifies, then writes preparation.json.

parse_mps (tools/prepare_affine.py:20-60), a Python MPS reader that assigns ids in appearance order ('id':len(vars) at :41), is referenced 179 times across tools/*.py; no preparer reads the kernel's canonical model or exported model JSON.
friction: No public proof-construction API: this 177-line case preparer sits on a 999-line transitive stack of sibling preparers and hand-emits 66,638 + 20,441 top-level steps, 467,436 linear terms and 154,589 Return checks as Python dicts.

Scope is data, but its selection is not derived: :171 hardcodes input_integers/output_integers true for both claims, and nothing in the RPA, request or audit records that the load-bearing 13,750 alias eliminations are integrality-only, so flipping the flag yields an unprovable LP-strength claim with no build-time signal.

Obligation enumeration is manual and order-critical: the preparer must reproduce the kernel's fixed Return order (bounds, ints, rows, objective, projections, inverse) and the 'Exact' shortcuts; with 154,589 entries and no partial acceptance, one surplus or missing witness rejects a 17.9 MB certificate.

The contract is emitted twice verbatim (175,996 B RPA claims array == request.json), 99.9% of it a hand-built 6,846-pair projection table per claim while the scope decision itself is 107 B of flags; corpus contracts differ (62 of 80 request.json files contain input_integers:false, e.g. cases/test11 claim 2), so the flags are a per-case choice.

Representation bookkeeping is hand-rolled: a 24-line liveness pass (drop_dead, which must model inherited branch references through ChainMap) emits 23,322 Drop steps / 25,094 ids (568,138 B), and 6,875 structurally identical Cases steps cost 7,288,065 B (40.7% of the RPA) because nothing in the API batches or templates them.
